subject.title: ci: accept trusted unsigned release merge heads

question: Should Full Release Validation intentionally trust an unsigned exact release-branch merge head using unique merged-PR attribution and the merger's current maintain or admin permission?
rationale: This substitutes an authorization-and-attribution policy for a missing cryptographic signature, so repository automation cannot safely choose the permanent release trust model.

options.title: Approve after boundary proof
options.body: Accept the constrained unsigned-merge rule after an exact-head run or executable payload matrix demonstrates the intended acceptance and fail-closed rejection cases.

options.title: Require signed release heads
options.body: Retain signed-only provenance and change the release merge process to produce a GitHub-verifiable signature.

recommendation.title: Approve after boundary proof
recommendation.body: Accept the constrained unsigned-merge rule after an exact-head run or executable payload matrix demonstrates the intended acceptance and fail-closed rejection cases.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is directly connected to the rejected release candidate, current release operations, and the proposed trust-policy correction.
